# Day 4: Scientific Writing: Title, Abstract, Intro, Methods, Results, Conclusion

## Topic of the Day

Scientific Writing: Title, Abstract, Intro, Methods, Results, Conclusion

## Assigned Readings

Because scientific publishing combines framing, hypothesis-building, and responsible AI use, today includes additional readings.

1. [IMRaD structure in biomedical journals ↗](https://www.springernature.com/gp/authors/campaigns/writing-a-manuscript/structuring-your-manuscript)

2. [Writing Is Thinking ↗](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44222-025-00323-4)

3. [Thinking Is Not Only Writing ↗](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44222-026-00447-1)

4. [What’s Your Hypothesis? ↗](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-026-03104-y)

5. [How to Develop Good Research Questions ↗](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41562-025-02292-5)

6. [Using AI Responsibly in Scientific Publishing ↗](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-026-03020-1)

7. [Is it OK for AI to write science papers? Nature survey shows researchers are split](https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-025-01463-8)

8. [Should researchers use AI to write papers? Group aims for community-driven standards](https://doi10.1126/science.z9gp5zo)

9. [How much of the scientific literature is generated by AI?](https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-025-03504-8)

10. [Hallucinated citations are polluting the scientific literature. What can be done?](https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-00969-z)
